column1: # Step 4 (04-session-entry-point): what each scored family is worth.
# Since 2026-10-13 (user decision, product scoring) the two families are
# multiplied, not added: reward = T1 x T2, where T1 is the migrated family's
# points over its total weight below and T2 is the behavior family's points
# over its total weight below (score.py, product_reward). The weights still
# sum to 1; they now set the proportions inside each factor. Where the prose
# below speaks of a family's share of the reward, read it as that family's
# share before this change.
# Two families, as rule 5 requires, and neither below ~30%:
#   behavior   0.34   the tree still does what it did      replay + the repo's own tests
#   migrated   0.66   the build resolves Spark 3.3.4, every entry point is
#                     derived from a SparkSession, and ANSI is on deliberately
# The same .34/.66 balance steps 2 and 3 settled on, re-split inside itself.
# --- why three requirements here, and why m3 is one of them ------------------
# Step 3 learned the expensive version of this lesson (NOTES 6.3.11): at replay
# time the jobs run the *verifier image's* Spark, because spark-core is
# `provided`, the shaded jar does not carry it, and the replay's spark-submit is
# /opt/spark/bin/spark-submit. So any requirement whose only evidence is a
# session property the image already sets is a requirement nobody can fail, and
# step 3 had two of them priced at 0.14 before it measured them.
# That test was run against every candidate requirement here before this file
# was written (NOTES 6.4.4), and it disqualified one and kept one:
#   spark.sql.storeAssignmentPolicy   already ANSI on all 123 probe rows of the
#                                     do-nothing tree -- free, so it is a cheat
#                                     rule in cheats4.tsv, not a requirement
#   spark.sql.ansi.enabled            false on all 123 rows of the do-nothing
#                                     tree, and the harness's only setconf key
#                                     is spark.sql.warehouse.dir -- earnable
# So m3 is graded, and it is graded on `setconf` as well as `conf`: `setconf`
# comes from `conf.getAll()` filtered to spark.sql.* (GateProbe.java:441), which
# is the *application's* SparkConf. A value set at the builder shows there; the
# image's default and a post-hoc `spark.conf.set` do not. That is what makes the
# requirement "ANSI is on because this tree asked for it" rather than "ANSI is
# on".
# m1 is priced at 0.10, the lowest of the three, and honestly: only its two pom
# rules read something the candidate supplied. Its two session rules read the
# image, exactly as step 3's did, and they are kept for step 3's reason -- they
# cost nothing and would still catch a tree that forced a different Spark onto
# the submit line. m1 is not demoted to a standing rule the way step 3's m3/m4
# were, because unlike those, half of it is genuinely candidate-answered.
# m2 carries 0.44, the substance of the step: 63 sites in src/main construct a
# SparkConf and hand it to a JavaSparkContext, and the move is to derive the
# context from a SparkSession instead. This is the requirement a pom-only tree
# cannot touch.
# Measured rather than reasoned. The handed-tree figure is already in hand,
# because step 3's golden tree *is* step 4's do-nothing tree; the gate was run
# against it with all five scanners on real facts (NOTES 6.4.4):
#   the tree the agent is handed    0.00   measured end to end: m1, m2 and m3
#                                          all red (151 PASS / 9 FAIL / 0
#                                          ERROR, and all 9 are this step's own
#                                          requirements), and `session_adopted`
#                                          False, so the behaviour family is
#                                          not graded and the reward is 0.000
#                                          rather than 0.34. The earlier
#                                          hand-assembled reading of this same
#                                          tree said 146/11 (NOTES 6.4.4); the
#                                          three that moved are the two m1
#                                          session rules and `probe-submit-ok`,
#                                          all three of which need real probe
#                                          facts a hand-assembled set cannot
#                                          carry, and none of which changes the
#   pom.xml edited and nothing else  0.10   measured: m1 only (the pom pair goes
#                                          green, the session pair was already
#                                          green), m2 and m3 red, behaviour
#                                          gated to 0. Inside 4.3's "<= ~30%"
#   the golden solution              1.00   measured: migrated 0.66, behaviour
#                                          0.34, no rule red and no standing
#                                          rule tripped
# Four cheat trees were measured alongside them (NOTES 6.4.7): a tree that
# deletes the 63 confs and builds nothing in their place scores 0.22, one that
# routes every consolidated entry point through a factory rather than through
# its own session scores the same 0.22, and the two that reach the requirement
# through reflection or by loosening the store-assignment policy score 0.00 --
# both of those on a VOID, having earned 1.00 before the standing rules read it.
# Item 4.3 first calibrated three *counted* thresholds in m04.tsv, and the
# static review's round 1 retired all three (NOTES 6.4.8). Two facts about
# those measurements are why. `m2-session-adopted atleast:90` read 54 builder
# call sites on the handed tree and 102 on the golden one -- and a call site is
# not a program: one unused class with thirty-six builders in it -- 36 being
# just what 90 less the handed tree's own 54 comes to -- clears any threshold
# in that range while forty-seven entry points still have none.
# `m3-ansi-set`/`m3-ansi-effective` at `atleast:70` read 0 and 97 -- and 97 is
# not 124 because 16 of the golden tree's 113 live sessions belong to the
# suite's own HarnessDriver, which no candidate edits, so the threshold had to
# be set low enough to tolerate rows the candidate does not own and was
# therefore also low enough to tolerate rows the candidate *does* own being
# wrong.
# All three are now `absent` over per-compilation-unit and per-probe-file
# derived facts, which is the only rule shape an extra row cannot help:
#   m2-session-adopted   `ast.unit` carries (mains, sessions) per file. 78
#                        files under src/main declare a `public static void
#                        main` in both trees; 48 of them build no session on
#                        the handed tree and 0 do on the golden one. What
#                        counts as a session built was narrowed by the review's
#                        round 2 from a bare `builder()` call to a
#                        `getOrCreate()` whose receiver chain starts at
#                        `SparkSession.builder()`; both trees read the same
#                        either way (NOTES 6.4.9).
#   m2-session-live      `probe.appsession` is one row per program of this
#                        repository that the replay ran: 96 of the 123 probe
#                        files, the other 27 being the suite's HarnessDriver.
#                        29 of the handed tree's 96 bring up no session at all;
#                        all 96 of the golden tree's do.
#   m3-ansi-set          `probe.appsetconf` is what that program's own session
#                        was built with: 67 `<unset>` and 29 `<no-session>` on
#                        the handed tree, 96 `true` on the golden one.
#   m3-ansi-effective    `probe.appconf` is what the engine it ran in reported:
#                        67 `false` and 29 `<no-session>` on the handed tree,
#                        96 `true` on the golden one.
# The HarnessDriver problem disappears with the threshold rather than being
# tolerated: probe-derive.py drops those rows before the rule ever sees them,
# so "every program" can mean every program.
# Steps 2 and 3 gate the behaviour family on a milestone, because a tree that
# did not make the move preserves behaviour trivially and the marks are for a
# tree that made it. Step 4 needs it for the sharpest version of that reason
# yet: rung 04 is behaviourally silent on this codebase -- §6.4.1 measures
# c04 -> c05b as SAME on all 140 recordings and §6.4.2 measures the test suite as
# byte-identical with ANSI forced on -- so a tree that bumps one line of pom.xml
# replays 140/140 and passes the suite.
# `session_adopted` in score.py is this step's milestone: true when the gate
# reports no `SparkConf` constructed anywhere in src/main and none referenced
# from the jar, **and** `m2-session-adopted` green -- no file under src/main
# with a `public static void main` in it and no `SparkSession` built in the
# same file -- **and** `m2-session-live` green, no program the replay ran
# having come up without reaching one. All three parts read the same gate
# report m2 is scored from, and the rule ids and their modes are parsed out of
# m04.tsv rather than kept as a second copy here, so that "m2 happened" cannot
# come to mean two different things in two files.
# Why the conjunction rather than any one of them. The `no SparkConf` part
# alone is bought by deleting the 63 constructions and leaving the mains
# without a context -- which loses the replay, but would keep the .34 if
# behaviour were ungated, and breaking output is the failure mode this whole
# task exists to catch. The `sessions built` part alone is bought by adding a
# builder beside a SparkConf that is still there, which is the tree that read
# the instruction and did not do it. And the two of them together are bought by
# a tree whose sources carry the idiom in every one of the 78 files and whose
# programs never execute it -- the builder behind a branch that is false, or
# after the work it was meant to configure, or in a class the jar does not
# invoke. `m2-session-live` is what asks the run, and the static review's round
# 2 added it to this gate for that reason (NOTES 6.4.9). None of the three is
# the claim on its own.
# The second half is the one that needed a measurement to be worth anything.
# The handed tree already calls `SparkSession.builder` 54 times in src/main,
# because an earlier step added a session to 15 demos without retiring their
# SparkConf (NOTES 6.4.3) -- so any rule that merely counts those calls is a
# requirement partly satisfied by work this step did not do, and one that a
# single class full of builders satisfies outright. What the handed tree does
# not have is a session in each of its 48 conf-only entry points, and that is
# what the rule asks: `absent` over `ast.unit` rows whose file is under
# src/main, whose `main` count is non-zero and whose session count is 0.
# score.py carries the handed tree's 48 as `HANDED_MAINS_WITHOUT_SESSION` and
# `session_rule_ids` refuses any `-session-adopted` rule that is not that
# shape -- not `absent`, not over `ast.unit`, not scoped to src/main, or not
# asking for a session count of zero -- so the floor cannot be lowered by
# editing the rule file alone. The third part is guarded the same way and for
# the same reason: `HANDED_PROGRAMS_WITHOUT_SESSION` is the 29 of 96, and a
# `-session-live` rule that is not `absent`, that reads some fact other than
# the per-program `probe.appsession`, or that accepts a value other than `true`
# is refused, because each of those is green on the tree the agent is handed.
# score.py's selftest rehearses every one of those refusals and
# rehearse-step04.sh rehearses three of them against doctored copies of the
# real file -- the count shape being the exact text that was on disk before the
# review.
# What it costs, stated rather than hidden: the item-6 floor -- step 3's
# finished solution scored by this verifier -- reports 0.0 rather than the .34 an
# ungated behaviour family would pay it. That is the 0.00 measured above, it
# satisfies item 6's "<= 0.5" with room, and it is right for the reason it was
# right at steps 2 and 3: step 4 is not paid for step 3's work at all, which is
# what `hold m03.tsv` means.
# Within `migrated`, a requirement scores all or nothing: every rule carrying
# its prefix must be PASS. For m1 that is trivially right -- "mostly at 3.3.4"
# is not a state a build can be in. For m3 it is right because the claim is
# uniformity: `m3-ansi-no-dissent` exists so that a tree which sets ANSI on most
# sessions and explicitly false on one does not collect the requirement, and a
# proportional score would have paid it for the majority.
# The static review's rounds 1 and 2 both raised the same consequence of that
# choice and it is recorded here rather than argued away: a candidate who lands
# on 3.3.4, consolidates 40 of the 63 entry points and sets ANSI on those 40
# scores 0.10 -- the same as a candidate who edited one line of pom.xml and
# stopped. migration_prompt.md's rule 8 asks for proportional credit, and what
# this file pays proportionally is the behaviour family: the replay is credited
# per block over 140 jobs and the suite per test over 140 tests. Inside a
# requirement the credit is all-or-nothing, across the three requirements it is
# not, and both documents the candidate reads say so in those words. The
# alternative -- paying m2 per file migrated -- was measured against the trees
# in NOTES 6.4.7 and rejected there: it would pay a tree whose 23 untouched
# entry points still build their own SparkConf more than the `nosession` tree
# that at least ends up internally consistent, and it would make the behaviour
# gate a threshold again, which is what round 1 retired. The cliff is real,
# it is disclosed, and it is the price of the milestone being a milestone.
# For m2 it is the substantive choice, and it is deliberate. Sixty-two of the 63
# sites migrated is not 62/63 of the move: the one left behind still builds its
# own SparkConf, which means the step's actual claim -- that configuration is
# set in one place per main and the entry point is derived from it -- is false
# for that program. The 63 sites are also not 63 copies of one edit; 15 files
# already carry both a SparkConf and a SparkSession (NOTES 6.4.3), so in those
# the migrator has to retire the conf and re-point the context at the session
# that is already there, rather than add a session.
# Within `behavior`, credit is proportional and the unit is rule 7's scored
# input. The suite's denominator is 140 and not step 3's 142:
# `StructType.toString()` dropped a space between 3.2.4 and 3.3.4 and
# CustomReportServiceTest hardcodes the old rendering, so its two tests are red
# at this rung for every tree including the golden one -- test.sh replaces
# /app/src/test with the commit's own copy before the suite runs, so a
# candidate's correction is deleted before it can be scored. Scoring them would
# cap the oracle at 0.9986 and, worse, pay the same for deleting the file as for
# repairing it. They leave both baselines and come back as a precondition
# (NOTES 6.4.2). The recordings are the c05b census: the same tree at Spark 3.3.4, JDK 8,
# Scala 2.12 -- this step's own rung, because a step that moves the runtime must
# be graded against recordings made on the runtime it runs on.
# 32m53s, from this step's verifier container starting to its reward.json: the
# oracle run of 2026-09-19 (jobs dir m27-s4-oracle, job
# 27-spark24-to-4.0__QVT3WTN), at cpus = 7, on a box shared with another
# agent's jobs, so it is a loaded reading rather than a clean one. The same run
# scored steps 1, 2 and 3 at 29m25s, 30m07s and 30m36s. Rule 10 aims at ~30
# minutes a step and caps at 60; this is inside the cap and just over the aim,
# and the estimate that stood here before it was taken -- "the same place as
# step 3" -- was right to within four minutes.
# The 140-job replay is the bulk of it, and neither it nor the 46-class suite is
# reducible without asking a smaller question: rule 10's own instruction is not
# to shrink a fixture set to fit a clock. The same tree scored by run-verifier.sh
# on this box, outside Harbor, takes 28m19s; the difference is the image start,
# the artifact hand-off and the second agent.
# This paragraph names the run before it rather than the run that certifies it.
# A payload cannot cite the run that measures the package containing it -- the
# citation would change the package, which would invalidate the run. The run
# taken against these bytes is m27-s4-oracle-rebuilt, and it is recorded in
# NOTES-authoring.md rather than here (the same regress step 3 walked out of).
# family
